title: We Bet You Didn’t Know All 25 Of These Things About Ocarina Of Time
description: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a faithful remake, but that doesn't mean it can't pack a few surprises. Between updates and modernizations, and just the way some new systems interact, there are a fair number of secrets and strange interactions to uncover throughout the land of Hyrule. Some of these were there in the original and have been kept intact, while others have been updated to have slightly different effects. Then there are some that are new to this version of the game, ready for curious adventurers to uncover. We've rounded up 25 of them below, and there are surely still many more to discover. For example, the Easter egg you can see through the window of Hyrule Castle has been changed slightly, and the Mask of Truth gives us extra insight to the inner lives of Hyrulians. That leads to a shocking revelation about one NPC in particular that I won't spoil. "For fans, to play this remake is to remember over and over again why you fell in love with Ocarina in the first place, and to see the brilliance with fresh eyes," says to our Ocarina of Time review. "For newcomers, this is now the definitive way to experience this all-time classic, and it’s a can’t-miss Switch 2 exclusive for everyone else." Ocarina of Time currently sits at a 96 on GameSpot sister site Metacritic, making it the highest-reviewed game of 2026 so far.

title: CoD: Warzone’s New Intro Mode Lets Players Buy A Nuke, Which Isn’t Very Beginner-Friendly
description: Modern Warfare 4 has integrated with Warzone for Season 1, bringing new maps, modes, and game mechanics to Call of Duty's battle royale. The season introduces a brand-new training mode called Rally Point, which oddly enough, also lets players buy the game-ending nuke killstreak that's normally reserved for multiplayer. This is the first time Warzone has let players buy a nuke, but this seems like an odd choice for a training ground designed to allow players the space to learn, as sweaty players are joining the lobby just to nuke them. Warzone's Rally Point takes place on the new Zodiac Resurgence map as a casual game mode with a mix of 20 players and bots. There is no time limit or circle collapse, so it doesn't play quite like a traditional match, but it means players are free to take their time and explore the entirety of the map. Respawns are also unlimited, so everyone can die and respawn as much as they want. Profanity warning for the video clip shared below. In the Season 1 blog post, Activision describes Rally Point as a "training ground experience" for Warzone, and it encourages players to explore and learn within this new mode. "Rally Point aims to be an experience that allows players to experiment with Call of Duty: Warzone’s mechanics and systems, while also providing unique elements to play around with," the publisher said. Activision's description makes Rally Point sound like a mode designed to onboard new players, or allow returning players to more freely learn the movement and new mechanics added with Modern Warfare 4's integration. However, Warzone's Buy Stations allows players to purchase a game-ending Tactical Nuke killstreak for the steep price of one million dollars. Players can also use Buy Stations to purchase more practically priced items, such as self-revives, perks, and typical Warzone killstreaks, but adding a nuke into a training mode seems like an oversight. A $1 million price tag isn't easy to achieve in Warzone, even if a full squad…

title: Can You Upgrade To GTA 6’s $100 Edition? Yes, And It’s Easy–Here’s How
description: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 launches on November 19. If you're planning to buy the $80 edition but want to upgrade later to the $100 version, you might be interested to know if such a thing is possible. Thankfully, yes, it is-and it's very easy to do. Rockstar will offer an "Ultimate Edition Upgrade" for $20, so for anyone who buys the $80 version and decides they do want the additional perks, they can upgrade. This applies to both the digital edition of GTA 6 that you can buy from the Xbox and PlayStation stores, as well the code-in-a-box physical edition. You can get a haircut like this at Sara's Unisex Hair Salon, which is exclusive to the $100 edition. The $100 Ultimate Edition, which is not sold in stores, includes a lot of extras, including vehicles, weapons, clothing for your in-game characters. The items are "threaded across all aspects of Jason and Lucia's story," Rockstar said, with new items becoming available "behind each chapter." Additionally, people who buy the $100 version get access to in-game businesses that won't be available to everyone else, including a hair salon, a tattoo parlor, a mod shop, and more. Meanwhile, all preorders for GTA 6 come with the The Vintage Vice City Pack and one month of GTA+. In other news, preloading for GTA 6 begins November 10, and that's good news considering the game weighs in at a whopping 212GB. The game officially unlocks at midnight local time, so pack your bags for New Zealand if you want to play it sooner.

title: Looking at Xbox, You Can See Everything
description: Like many people who have watched Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s masterful documentary You Can See Everything, I sat down with my friend after our screening to bounce our thoughts off of one another. The film revolves around convicted felon Elizabeth Holmes, the former CEO of Theranos who was criminally indicted for defrauding investors, and her husband Billy Evans, who met her some time after the charges against Holmes were made, picking up their story a month before her incarceration. The documentary is about a lot of things, but at its core, the main question it posits is whether Holmes is a master manipulator or is being masterfully manipulated by the men in her life, with multiple parallels drawn between her husband Evans and her former partner, both romantically and in business at Theranos, Ramesh "Sunny" Balwani. At the end of the conversation I was having with my friend, I came to the conclusion that it was a Schrodinger’s Cat kind of situation; Holmes is both a master manipulator and has found herself in partnerships with other master manipulators, and therefore, she is always manipulating but also always being manipulated, all at once. I then came to a more straightforward answer: You Can See Everything is about two people whose heads are so firmly up their own asses, and each other's asses, that they form an ouroboros, with no way to tell where one of them begins and the other ends. On the subway ride home from the theater, I was going over the news that I had missed in the day, including Microsoft’s latest financial report, which revealed that, once again, Xbox hardware revenue had declined year-over-year. Following this announcement, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma gave a similar explanation that she has used in the past, saying the reason sales were down was due to a lack of supply of Xbox consoles to meet demand. In such close proximity to viewing You Can See Everything, a three-hour film that lays bare, quite literally in one scene, what delusion looks…

title: Donuts Beat AI: Nvidia Has Lost $1 Trillion+ In The Past Month, While Krispy Kreme Surges
description: Following the US midterm elections this week, shares of Nvidia--the world's No. 2 most valuable company by market cap behind Apple--slid downhill in a big way. In fact, more than $1 trillion has been wiped out from Nvidia's market cap since its peak in October. Nvidia stock rebounded today, November 6, following the huge selloff on November 5 that also affected numerous other AI and technology stocks. However, Nvidia is still lagging behind Krispy Kreme in terms of growth in 2026. Krispy Kreme's stock exploded this week. That's right, shares of Krispy Kreme stock--$DNUT--are up about 3% in 2026, compared to negative returns for Nvidia this year. If you invested $1,000 into both $DNUT and $NVDA this year, you'd be making money on donuts and losing money on AI. Krispy Kreme's stock price exploded on November 5 after a solid earnings report, but has moderated since. In any event, Krispy Kreme is beating Nvidia so far in 2026 based on the percent gain for its stock price. To be sure, Nvidia and Krispy Kreme are not competitors in the market and their stock prices are not comparable except for the purpose of some laughs. Nvidia, with a market cap of more than $4.5 trillion, remains a juggernaut that captures the world's attention. Krispy Kreme, meanwhile, has a market cap of under $1 billion, but they do make a damn good glazed donut. Krispy Kreme also rolled out a new line of Pokemon donuts this year, and they're delicious. The Nvidia selloff was due in part to Democrats taking control of the House and Senate--that's notable because a lot of candidates who won seats are campaigning against AI data centers, thereby putting pressure on Nvidia's stock price. Alternatively, lawmakers don't seem to have any issues with donuts.

title: You Can Finally Drive A Dreamcast, Thanks To Sonic
description: Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds is gearing up for a second year of action, and while you can expect new courses, modes, and characters to join the game, the real headline act here is the new cars coming to it. As part of the Sega Consoles Pack, players will be able to tear around courses while driving a four-wheeled Sega video game console, with each vehicle expertly blending the design of that classic gaming hardware into a lean-and-mean racing machine. The new cars are based on the Sega Genesis (or Mega Drive for anyone who lived outside the US), the Sega Saturn, and Sega's final home console, the Dreamcast. According to the Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds development team, the idea was to incorporate design elements that would instantly remind players of each console into their respective vehicle frames, like the rounded form of the Dreamcast or the angular silhouettes and subdued tones of the Saturn. The team even went so far as to recreate the Dreamcast’s Visual Memory Unit using original reference data from that era. "Rather than directly recreating the hardware itself, we translated rounded forms into fenders and nose sections, while angular lines became body panels and hoods, adding the sense of speed expected from a racing machine," the development team explained in a PlayStation Blog post. "While preserving recognizable colors and components from each system, we also designed around the game’s front-and-rear combination mechanic, incorporating the fun of pairing consoles and controllers into the vehicles themselves." The end result is a design that instantly clues you in on which console informed its design, while still looking like it can burn some rubber on the track. Sega said that the "Genesis Tower" proved to be challenging and required considerable experimentation so that it wouldn't interfere with various visual elements, but it managed to nail the design in the end. In addition to the Sega Console cars, Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds will also get a new Duel Mode…

title: There’s A New DMZ Map Hidden In MW4, And Here’s How To Find It
description: Season 1 of Modern Warfare 4 adds a brand-new DMZ map, but it isn't accessible from the menus. In this DMZ guide, we'll show you how to find the entrance to X01 on Hajin, and we'll provide some tips to help you survive this new extraction experience in Modern Warfare 4. What is the X01 map in MW4 DMZ mode? X01 building X01 is a smaller DMZ map set within a weapons facility near the northern border of North Korea. This map is designed for close-quarters engagements, which is similar to the Building 21 map from the DMZ beta in 2022. X01 features exclusive DMZ gear and resources, and it might even house a secret Easter egg quest, as well. This is Modern Warfare 4's most dangerous DMZ experience yet, so we'll give you all our best tips for surviving. How to access the hidden X01 map X01 is located in the northwest tip of Hajin, as marked with a yellow ping. While this is a separate map for DMZ, the elevator entrance is hidden within the main Hajin map. There are different ways to travel to the entrance of X01, but the quickest way to reach this northwestern point of the map is to select the Iron Citadel story mission when you infil into DMZ, as this will guarantee you a spawn close to the hidden elevator. You don't even need to complete this story mission. Just head straight to the X01 entrance as marked in the image above, which is the northwestern tip of Hajin. Obviously, you can access the area by loading into a free roam match or by choosing Dynamic Ops, but you'll likely want to grab a vehicle straight away. This is going to be a popular area, so you want to get there before everyone else can meet you at the entrance. This area is a large building with a gated entrance on the right-hand side. Interact with a button on the wall to open the gate, and then head inside the elevator on the right. If you're in a squad, all players must select the option to ready up and enter this new location. title: Mass Effect Is Getting A New Art Collection At A Difficult Time For Its Fans
description: This year's annual Mass Effect Day looks to be somber in light of the studio behind the games, BioWare, being shut down last month. But while no new Mass Effect games are currently on the horizon, you can celebrate its legacy through some classy art prints that are going up for sale ahead of N7 Day. Preorders for the Mass Effect Collection will begin on Friday, November 6, at 10 AM PT / 1 PM ET / 6 PM BST on the Moor-Art website. The Mass Effect Collection Moor-Art says it began collaborating with BioWare over a year ago to release a new selection of limited-edition posters. "What began as a celebration of an ongoing saga now feels like the bastion in the continuation of a studio's legacy," the studio said in a press release. The collection from Moor-Art is inspired by the characters and worlds of Mass Effect, with the original artwork being produced by acclaimed artists and Mass Effect die-hard fans Matt Essom and Dan Mumford. The designs will also be available as T-shirts. The first one is by Essom, and Moor-Art says this illustration captures the spirit and emotional depth of the series, as well as the bonds forged on the Normandy as her crew traveled to unknown worlds. This will be limited to 200 hand-numbered prints worldwide, plus 30 Giclée prints with a certificate of authenticity signed by the artist. Mumford's "Mass Effect 2" poster aims to capture the sci-fi horror elements of the confrontations against the Reapers, and it features a full ensemble of crew members. As an added touch, it'll be available in two distinct editions: one with the Normandy crew being led by the version of Commander Shepard, while the other one swaps him out for FemShep. Only 150 hand-numbered prints for each variant will be produced, alongside 30 Giclée prints of each Shepard variant, with a certificate of authenticity signed by the artist. If you miss out on both of these prints, you can grab them as T-shirts, either to wear or to frame--or both! Meanwhile, EA announced a new…

title: The Best Warzone Perks May Surprise You After The MW4 Overhaul
description: Modern Warfare 4 integrates with Warzone for Season 1, adding MW4's full weapon pool, attachments, and other new gear into battle royale. The big update also overhauls Warzone's perk system, including the introduction of the powerful new "Elite" perks. In this guide, we'll explain how perks work for this new year of Warzone and include some recommended picks for your next match. How perks work in Warzone for MW4 For Modern Warfare 4, there are a total of 18 perks available for Warzone. The first 15 are options you can choose for your custom loadouts, fitting into one of three different perk slots. The remaining three are new Elite perks, and you can acquire one during a match as an additional fourth perk. Elite perks are a special perk type that are only discoverable within a match. These can be gained through various means, including Buy Station purchases or as rewards for completing Supply Run contracts. Only one Elite Perk can be equipped at a time. Additionally, Tactical Sprint is no longer a perk this year and everyone will have this movement be default. Warzone's new create-a-class menu All perk 1 options Field Medic This perk allows you to quickly revive allies to full health, and you gain the same benefits. You also receive increased health while downed. Hunter Hunter lets you track enemy footprints, sense nearby enemies, and become alert when aimed at. It also outlines enemies you shoot for a duration. Stocked This perk lets you carry an additional lethal and tactical equipment item and see a visible trajectory when you throw it. It deals increased explosive damage from equipment and launchers. When pulled from a loadout drop, it also provides full ammo reserves for your primary and secondary weapons. Incognito As the name suggests, Incognito helps keep you off the enemy radar. It reduces the duration you are revealed on radar and the marked Hunter outline. You can only be danger pinged by enemies, and you delay any traps you trigger. Surveyor On kill,…

title: Airframe Ultra's PS1 cyberpunk city is an amazing tribute to G-Police and WipEout, and I wish you people would slow down to appreciate it
description: I do not wish to "rule the streets" of Megacity West, dear creators of Airframe Ultra. I wish to be ravished by them, rubbing my face against the rusty corrugated metal of the shipping containers, and savouring the acid blue waters of the bay. I do not want to "become the one thing with freedom in a city of billions: A racer." I want to become the other thing with freedom in a city of billions: a person who slowly drives or – whisper it - walks around just looking at stuff, because gadzooks, this is one of the prettiest PS1 cyberpunk burgs I've laid eyes on. Those eroded pastel chevrons. Those seductively wobbling vertices. That electric reef of a downtown backdrop, murderously luring your gaze from the on-coming trucks. That layer of invigorating crackle over everything. Every moment or so, I dismount from my hoverbike to inspect some concrete ruin I could swear I last saw in G-Police, or ponder the resemblance between a subway tunnel and WipEout 2097's Gare d'Europa. Then, somebody waps me in the skull with a stop sign at 300 kilometres an hour. But I was already stopped, frantic stranger! Your brutal poetic ironies are wasted on me. Read more
